issues.where: ClonerDepthEcho.tsx, stage wrapper (position:absolute; left: 960-260; transformStyle preserve-3d) inside <FaRoot> (direction:rtl); frames f0, f45, f68, f119
issues.problem: FaRoot's direction:rtl changes the static position of the absolutely positioned child divs (clones and hero have no left/right). They anchor to the right edge of the zero-width stage box and the cards extend leftwards. The hero card renders at x~112..698 instead of the original x~700..1190, so the whole composition is shoved to the far left under a centered title, and the right half of the frame is empty. The clone queue (spreading up and to the right) is cramped against the left edge. report.json claims 'all constants unchanged', but the visual centering of the original is lost.
issues.suggestedFix: Give the stage wrapper a fixed width:520 (or give every absolute child left:0 / insetInlineStart:0, or set direction:'ltr' on the 3D stage) so the hero card is again centered at x=960 as in the original (compare orig f0: card spans 700..1190). Then re-check f45: the queue should fan out to the upper right of a centered card and stay in frame.

issues.where: Card placeholder internals (Fixtures Card), frames f0/f45
issues.problem: Card contents are mirrored by the inherited RTL direction (title bars right-aligned, avatar and line at bottom-right), whereas the original has them left-aligned with the avatar at bottom-left. This is neither documented nor intentional: the header and report state the Card is 'reused unchanged' and has 'no directional meaning'. It does mirror correctly for RTL in principle, but the author did not decide it, and the file's rtlDecisions entry is false.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide explicitly. Preferred: keep the mirrored content (valid for RTL UI placeholder) and document it in the header and report, or wrap the Card in direction:ltr to keep the original. Either way fix the claim.

issues.where: Direction decision for the diagonal queue (dx=+64*idx), header comment and report rtlDecisions
issues.problem: The clone fan goes up-right (visible in f45). With a correct centered layout this is a justifiable physical-depth choice, but the author never viewed the original later frames (only f0) and never verified the composition. Consider mirroring dx and rotateY sign (and perspectiveOrigin 58% -> 42%) so the echo trails toward the reading start (right side) for RTL balance; at minimum document the reasoning with evidence.
issues.suggestedFix: Either mirror dx to -64*idx, rotateY(-16deg), perspectiveOrigin '42% 46%' (keeping timing/z/dy), or keep it and justify after viewing a centered render.
